title: Architecture
text: agentsys architecture (current) One-page map of how the tool fits together as of the hardening baseline. Components Piece Role agentsys/store.py SQLite schema, task state machine, append-only events , findings, checkpoints, runs (per project), approvals agentsys/ledger.py User-level ~/.agentsys/ledger.db : budgets and run totals across all projects agentsys/cli.py All commands; dispatches to adapters; human-facing messages and resume brief agentsys/verify.py Verification gate: scope, syntax, secrets regex, task --check commands agentsys/budget.py Pre-run cap checks, estimates, alerts agentsys/adapters.py Headless runs: mock, cursor-agent, claude, codex, grok agentsys/gitops.py Worktrees, merge-check, merge agentsys/ui.py + ui.html Local dashboard; read state; optional writes via POST /api/action State machine Tasks move through guarded transitions ( TRANSITIONS in store.py ). Every transition runs in a transaction and appends an event. Terminal states: merged , cancelled . Dependencies must be accepted or merged before claim. Typical implement path: ready → in_progress (claim + lease) → submitted → verified (gate) → accepted (review) → merged (human approval + git merge). Stores Project store: <repo>/.agent-system/state.db (gitignored). Tasks, events, findings, checkpoints, runs for that repo. Ledger: AGENTSYS_LEDGER or ~/.agentsys/ledger.db . Budget rows and imported runs; shared caps apply no matter which project dispatches. On Store open, project runs/budgets are imported into the ledger idempotently. Identity model (today) Actors are self-declared strings: harness:account:role (e.g. codex:alice:work , human:vedansh ). The store enforces: Review: authors(tid) (claim/checkpoint/submit) cannot review. Approvals/merge: only human: actors in decide_approval . There is no cryptographic binding to a vendor login yet (Phase 1 adds tamper-evident logs and human-action refusals). Adapters agentsys dispatch builds a prompt (including AGENT_RULES ), checks budget, claims or continues work, runs the vendor CLI in the task worktree, records usage, writes output as a finding, checkpoints/submits or releases on failure. Verification gate agentsys verify runs verify.run_pipeline : allowed paths, syntax helpers, secret patterns (type only in reports), custom checks, and for research tasks at least one evidenced finding. Dashboard Stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1. Polls /api/state and /api/task . Writable mode requires per-page session token + matching Host/Origin.

title: Integrations
text: Integrating agentsys with coding agents Identity is always harness:account:role (or agent:harness:role for automation). The MCP server and CLI read identity from startup args / AGENTSYS_ACTOR , not from tool payloads. MCP (stdio) Run from the git project root (or pass --db ): Copy export AGENTSYS_ACTOR=cursor:alice:implementer agentsys mcp Exposed tools: claim , heartbeat , finding , checkpoint , submit , resume , status , list_tasks . There is no approve, merge, or human review tool. Cursor Cursor’s MCP client configuration format changes between releases. Point a custom MCP server at the command above if your build supports arbitrary stdio servers. We have not re-verified the exact mcp.json schema against current Cursor docs in this repo. Claude Code Claude Code documents project-level MCP servers under user settings; use the same agentsys mcp command with AGENTSYS_ACTOR=claude:you:work . Confirm paths in Anthropic’s latest Claude Code documentation before relying on this in production. Codex CLI OpenAI’s Codex CLI MCP wiring should mirror any stdio MCP server entry. Set AGENTSYS_ACTOR=codex:you:work . Treat config file names and flags as vendor-controlled. Grok Build Install the Grok Build CLI ( curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash ), run grok login , then use the same stdio MCP entry with AGENTSYS_ACTOR=grok:you:work . Headless dispatch uses agentsys dispatch <task> --adapter grok --account you . Routing rules (optional) Add routing.rules to .agentsys/profile.json (commit this file in your repo). Each rule matches a task kind ( research , implement , or * ) and lists prefer candidates in order. Routing checks that the CLI is installed, a budget exists, check_dispatch passes, and optional max_pct is not exceeded (uses the rolling window percent when set). Copy agentsys route t-abc12345 # print adapter, account, reason (no spend) agentsys dispatch t-abc12345 --adapter auto --account ignored Routing never bypasses per-account caps. Adapter health Copy agentsys adapters --check # offline: --version per CLI agentsys adapters --check --live --account you --adapter mock # tiny read-only prompt (spends quota) agentsys doctor includes an adapter-versions row from the offline check. Watch / scheduler (optional) Requires routing.rules in .agentsys/profile.json . Each tick reaps expired leases, picks ready tasks, and runs agentsys dispatch --adapter auto (or prints decisions with --dry-run ). Copy agentsys watch --once --dry-run agentsys watch --interval 120 --max-parallel 1 Task pipelines (optional) Define templates in .agentsys/profile.json or use the built-in research-implement template (research task, then implement with --path and --check ). Copy agentsys pipeline --list agentsys pipeline research-implement "Add dark mode" --path "src/*" --check "npm test" Review assignment (optional) Set review.pairs in .agentsys/profile.json to map author harness → reviewer harness ( "*" is the fallback). When require_different_harness is true (default), reviewers must use a different harness than anyone who claimed or submitted the task. Copy agentsys reviewer t-abc12345 Git hooks Copy export AGENTSYS_ACTOR=human:you agentsys hooks install Hooks call agentsys hooks merge-check and agentsys hooks push-check . Fast-forward merges do not run pre-merge-commit ; prefer git config merge.ff false or rely on pre-push plus CI check-branch . Human override (recorded in the event log): Copy agentsys check-branch agent/t-abc12345 --override-reason "hotfix" --as human:you Environment Variable Purpose AGENTSYS_ACTOR Default identity AGENTSYS_DB Store path AGENTSYS_LEDGER Shared usage ledger AGENTSYS_CLI Path used by git hooks (tests set this) AGENTSYS_DISPATCHED Set in adapter children; blocks forged human actions

title: CLI reference
text: CLI reference Generated from agentsys --help . Do not edit by hand; run python3 scripts/check_docs_drift.py --write . Copy usage: agentsys [-h] [--version] [--as ACTOR] [--db DB] {init,pipeline,task,show,claim,heartbeat,release,block,unblock,requeue,cancel,finding,checkpoint,submit,verify,review,merge-check,merge,approvals,approve,deny,status,log,resume,handoff,reviewer,route,dispatch,budget,usage,adapters,watch,doctor,metrics,demo,check-branch,hooks,mcp,profile,verify-log,approver,ui} ... Durable task coordination for multiple coding agents. positional arguments: {init,pipeline,task,show,claim,heartbeat,release,block,unblock,requeue,cancel,finding,checkpoint,submit,verify,review,merge-check,merge,approvals,approve,deny,status,log,resume,handoff,reviewer,route,dispatch,budget,usage,adapters,watch,doctor,metrics,demo,check-branch,hooks,mcp,profile,verify-log,approver,ui} init create the store for this repository pipeline create chained tasks from a template task create and list tasks show full task record as JSON claim claim a task (creates a worktree for implement tasks) heartbeat extend your lease release give a claimed task back block mark blocked (needs human/dependency) unblock return a blocked task to ready requeue return an escalated task to ready cancel cancel a task finding record a finding, artifact, decision, blocker or question checkpoint record progress (optionally commit the worktree) submit commit and hand the task to verification verify run the verification pipeline review independent review (reviewer must not have worked on the task) merge-check dry-run merge; detects conflicts without touching any tree merge merge an accepted task (requires human approval) approvals list approval requests approve grant an approval (human: actors only) deny deny an approval (human: actors only) status overview of tasks, approvals and budgets log audit trail resume self-contained brief to continue a task from its last verified checkpoint handoff resume brief plus the next dispatch command for a harness reviewer suggest reviewer harness from profile review.pairs route print adapter/account from profile routing rules (no dispatch) dispatch run a headless agent on a task, within budget budget per-account token limits usage self-report interactive usage adapters detect available agent CLIs watch dispatch ready tasks using routing rules doctor pass/warn/fail health table metrics local task/run counters demo scripted onboarding story (<30s) check-branch CI: exit 0 only if an agent/* branch is accepted or merged hooks install git hooks for agent/* branches mcp stdio MCP server (worker tools only) profile repo verification profile verify-log verify tamper-evident event hash chain approver optional passphrase for signed human approvals ui live dashboard on 127.0.0.1 (actions recorded as human:<you>) options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --version show program's version number and exit --as ACTOR identity, e.g. cursor:alice:implementer (or AGENTSYS_ACTOR) --db DB store path (default: <git root>/.agent-system/state.db, or AGENTSYS_DB)

title: Security
text: Security model Scope agentsys coordinates agents that run as the same local user . It provides guardrails against agent mistakes. It is not an isolation boundary against a malicious local process. Property Status Actor identity Self-declared ( --as ). Not authenticated. Store Local SQLite file, mode 0600 ; any process running as your user can write to it. Worktrees Separate files, not a sandbox. Agents can still reach paths outside them. Real sandboxing Delegated to each harness: codex --sandbox , cursor-agent --sandbox enabled , Claude Code --allowedTools / --permission-mode . Defaults Child processes get no provider API-key variables (see adapters.API_KEY_VARS ). codex runs read-only for research and workspace-write for implementation, with network off (the Codex default). cursor-agent uses --force only for implementation tasks, and always with --sandbox enabled . Prompts go to claude and codex over stdin. cursor-agent only accepts the prompt as an argument, so it is visible in ps to the same user; never put secrets in task text. The verification secret scan reports matches by type and never prints the matched value. Merges need a granted approval from a human: actor and refuse to run on a dirty main tree. Reporting Open a private security advisory on the repository, or contact the maintainer directly. Please don't file public issues for vulnerabilities.

title: Threat model
text: agentsys threat model (local-first demo / team tool) agentsys coordinates AI coding agents on one machine (or one trusted host). It is not a multi-tenant SaaS. Assumptions and limits below are intentional. Assets Task store ( .agent-system/state.db ): tasks, findings, approvals, append-only events. Install key ( ~/.agentsys/install.key ): HMAC key for the event hash chain (mode 0600 ). Optional approver verifier ( ~/.agentsys/approver.json ): scrypt hash of a passphrase; signatures on human approvals when enabled. Shared usage ledger ( AGENTSYS_LEDGER or default path): token budgets across projects. Git worktrees and branches : real code changes until merge. Trust boundaries Actor Trust level Human at keyboard + TTY, or human on dashboard with session token Can approve, deny, merge (with confirmations), cancel, requeue Agent CLI / MCP ( harness:account:role or agent:harness:role ) Can claim, work, submit, review if a different identity than authors Dispatched child process ( AGENTSYS_DISPATCHED=1 ) Cannot perform human:* actions Anyone with shell + write access to the store file Can bypass all software rules (see below) Controls (software) Hash-chained events — Tampering with prev_hash / event_hash or meta chain_prev_hash is detected by agentsys verify-log . Pre-migration rows are legacy and anchored. Human provenance — Human actions record TTY/dashboard/dispatch state; refused when dispatched or without TTY/token (except dashboard token path). TTY confirmation — Sensitive CLI actions read yes from /dev/tty , not piped stdin. Reviewer independence — Store rejects review by task authors; dashboard/API flag same_account_review when reviewer shares an account segment with a worker. Scope / verify gate — Implement tasks must pass automated checks before review (extended in later phases with project test profiles). Git hooks (when installed) — pre-merge-commit / pre-push + check-branch reduce accidental merges; fast-forward merges do not run pre-merge-commit — use merge.ff=false or rely on pre-push + CI. Out of scope / honest limits Same-user shell is root. A user who can run sqlite3 on the store or export AGENTSYS_ACTOR=human:… with a real TTY can impersonate a human. The chain detects after-the-fact edits, not motivated same-user fraud. Self-declared identities — AGENTSYS_ACTOR is asserted, not cryptographically bound to vendor accounts (adapters report usage where possible). Network — Dashboard binds to localhost by default; Host/Origin/token reduce rebinding and drive-by POSTs, not a stolen laptop session. Secrets in findings — Scanners reduce accidental commits; agents can still paste secrets into the DB if the human does not run verify-log and review. MCP and agents The stdlib MCP server exposes worker tools only (claim, heartbeat, finding, checkpoint, submit, resume, status). No approve, merge, or review-over-HTTP. Reporting incidents Run agentsys verify-log --strict on a copy of the store. Inspect events for unexpected human:* actors and same_account_review in the dashboard snapshot. Rotate approver passphrase ( agentsys approver init ) if passphrase may be compromised.

title: Contributing
text: Contributing Keep it dependency-free: Python ≥ 3.9 standard library only. Every behaviour change comes with a test in tests/ . Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v . Regenerate docs when CLI changes: python3 scripts/check_docs_drift.py --write . Regenerate the site changelog: python3 scripts/build_changelog_site.py . New adapters must report usage only as the provider's CLI actually emits it. If a CLI doesn't report usage, record usage_source="unknown" ; never invent numbers. Never add features that pool, rotate, or disguise accounts to get around provider limits.
